registration_scope: Repository-local procedural pre-registration authored before the first campaign execution; not externally timestamped.
study_stage: confirmatory within the declared toy task families
question: Can a fixed-size sparse event-driven state machine reduce continual sequence-update and memory-access cost relative to history-scanning attention without sacrificing transfer to exact delayed recall?

candidate.class: deterministic sparse event-driven machine with fixed persistent state and no external memory
candidate.rationale: Fixed state permits constant storage and sparse parity updates, offering a plausible memory-movement advantage on compressible streams.

baselines.scope: Stores every input and scans the retained history at query time; it is an algorithmic attention control, not a trained Transformer.
baselines.contamination_risk: None: exhaustive binary sequences are generated after the algorithms are fixed.

baselines.scope: Pre-registered for execution only if the candidate survives the information-theoretic recall falsifier.
baselines.planned_configuration: Decoder-only causal Transformer, 2 layers, 4 heads, d_model=64, seeds 0-9, trained on lengths 1-8 and held out on lengths 9-10 with version and hardware capture at execution.
baselines.contamination_risk: High unless held-out lengths and generated sequences remain inaccessible during training.

evaluation.replication: repeat the complete deterministic campaign and compare canonical result hashes
evaluation.uncertainty: No sampling uncertainty because enumeration is exhaustive; external-validity uncertainty remains unrestricted.

energy_boundary.prohibition: Do not infer joules, watts, or a 20 W path from logical counts.

falsifiers: Exact recall accuracy falls below 0.99 for any tested L greater than the fixed state-bit count.
A pigeonhole lower bound shows exact arbitrary L-bit recall requires at least L persistent information bits.
